## What does this PR do ?

Adds **dynamic context parallelism** on top of global-batch online packing (#6127, split out per review), with a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B fine-tuning recipe. With `model.dynamic_context_parallel=True`, Megatron-Core's `default_dynamic_cp` scheduler runs every packed microbatch on a context-parallel group sized for its longest sequence, chosen from the `dp × cp` pool, instead of splitting every microbatch across the full static group.

**Depends on #6127.** This branch contains that PR's commit; review the top commit only.

**Validation (`training/config.py`)**
- `model.dynamic_context_parallel` makes the dataset switch select `default_dynamic_cp`; setting either model field without `dataset.enable_global_batch_packing` is rejected.
- Dynamic-CP rules: a power-of-two `dp × cp` pool of at least two ranks, a power-of-two `min_dynamic_context_parallel_size` within the pool, `dist.use_decentralized_pg=False`, and `pool × max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` covering `seq_length`.
- The per-sequence alignment covers every group the pool can form: `2 × dp × cp`, and `dp × cp × tp` under sequence parallelism (review fix: the SP multiple previously ignored the DP factor and under-padded with TP above two and DP above one).
- The support probe requires the dynamic-CP arguments on the packed batch fetch and points at `./scripts/switch_mcore.sh dev` when they are missing.

**Glue and data**
- The packed batch fetch receives `dynamic_cp=True` only when dynamic CP is on; Megatron-Core returns a `PackedSeqParams` carrying the microbatch's CP group, which the glue binds before attention runs.
- `fold_alignment_padding` (GPT-SFT and `GPTDatasetConfig`) reports each sequence's alignment padding as part of the sequence. Set it when attention runs on FlashAttention under CP, for example head dimension 256 on Blackwell where Transformer Engine disables cuDNN fused attention for training: FlashAttention rejects THD bins with padding between sequences. It is exact for causal attention because the padding follows each sequence's last token and stays loss-masked. It also needs https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7417.

**Recipe, example, docs**
- `qwen35_text_35b_a3b_sft_8gpu_gb200_bf16_dynamic_cp_config`: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B SFT on CoderForge-Preview SWE-Rebench, TP1 PP1 CP4 EP8 on eight GB200 GPUs, 32K cap, 16 loader workers, full recompute (see Measured for why not selective).
- `examples/training_features/long_context/qwen35_35b_a3b_dynamic_cp.py` launches it, with a `--tiny-model` two-GPU smoke on a generated variable-length SFT file; the README shows measured results.
- New page `docs/training/dynamic-context-parallel.md` with its Fern mirror and navigation entries; `packed-sequences.md` stays global-batch-only.

Requires the Megatron-Core dev pin.

## Measured

**The recipe on GB200 (Bridge).** Eight GB200 GPUs in one NVL72 rack, NeMo 26.06.01, Megatron-Core dev pin + #7417, random initialization, the first 4,000 CoderForge SWE-Rebench trajectories, 12 steps with the first four dropped; throughput is Bridge's model TFLOP/s per GPU.

| Configuration | Median step | Median TFLOP/s per GPU | Peak allocated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recipe: dynamic CP, full recompute, 16 loader workers | 88 s | 90 | 108 GB |
| Static CP4 (`dp_balanced`), otherwise identical | 83 s | 93 | 108 GB |
| Recipe with 2 loader workers | 254 s | 31 | 108 GB |
| Recipe with selective recompute (`moe_act`, `layernorm`) | 75 s over four steps, then NCCL out of memory | 106 | 163 GB |

GPT-SFT tokenizes each CoderForge trajectory lazily (about 9 s per sample) and the scheduler pulls a whole step's samples at once, so the default two loader workers left the GPUs waiting; the recipe now sets 16. Selective recompute is about 13% faster per step but reserves over 170 GB per GPU, and the next communicator dynamic CP creates for a new group size then fails to allocate; full recompute keeps the headroom. About nine in ten of these trajectories exceed the 32K cap, so nearly every sequence needs the full CP4 group and dynamic CP stays within noise of static CP4 on this data. To check whether a longer cap changes that, I also ran 128K with CP8 and 16K tokens per rank, which keeps the trajectories whole: dynamic CP and static CP8 again stayed within noise (median step 188 s against 177 s, 81 against 83 TFLOP/s, peak 121 against 139 GB over steps 5 to 10), so the recipe keeps the 32K cap.

**Dynamic vs static CP on variable-length streams (Megatron-LM's loop).** Same Megatron-Core scheduler, measured earlier with Megatron-LM's training loop (dev `0c59fc6eb` + the `pad_between_seqs` fix, `pytorch:26.07-py3`, FlashAttention-2, 60% optimizer CPU offload), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on one GB200 node, TP1 PP1 CP4 EP4, full recompute, 10 iterations with the first 3 dropped:

| Stream | Cap / global batch | Static CP4 | Dynamic CP | Δ step time | Tokens eligible for CP1 / CP2 / CP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed-length SFT (median ~3.7K, tail to the cap) | 49,152 / 512 | 187.4 ± 10.6 s, 21.1K tok/s | **169.8 ± 14.7 s, 23.3K tok/s** | **−9.4%** | 38% / 22% / 39% |
| Near-cap RL (36K–46K) | 49,152 / 256 | 526.9 ± 3.7 s | 531.2 ± 6.2 s | +0.8% (tie) | 0 / 0 / 100% |
| Long RL (38K–97K) | 99,840 / 128 | 381.9 ± 14.4 s | 385.4 ± 35.5 s | +0.9% (tie) | 0 / 11% / 89% |

Dynamic CP pays where static CP is required by memory and the stream has short sequences to run on smaller groups; when every sequence needs the full group it is a small scheduling overhead, which matches the CoderForge result above.

**Loss parity, tiny smoke.** `--tiny-model` on two GPUs (CP2, EP2, MTP on), a generated variable-length SFT file, 6 steps:

| Step | Dynamic CP | Static CP2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.56843 | 12.56846 |
| 2 | 12.56869 | 12.56870 |
| 3 | 12.56614 | 12.56622 |
| 4 | 12.56872 | 12.56864 |
| 5 | 12.56307 | 12.56315 |
| 6 | 12.54839 | 12.54842 |

## Testing

- **Megatron-Core main pin (the CI configuration):** packing, config, step, eval, train, FLOPs, logging, GPT-SFT, builders, loaders, and recipe suites: 1,246 passed and 3 skipped (the dynamic-CP validation tests need the dev-pin config field). One failure, `test_native_energon_packing_allows_other_ep_dispatchers_with_fixed_width[flex]`, also fails on unmodified main on GB200.
- **Dev pin:** current main does not import against the pinned dev commit, because several modules import main-only Megatron-Core symbols (`set_default_log_ranks`, the GTP checkpoint-padding helpers, the FSDP V1/V2 adapter names, `save_tokenizer_assets`). To exercise this PR, I tested on the dev pin plus #7417 with those symbols backported from Megatron-Core main as a test-only shim. On that tree, all 38 global-batch packing and dynamic-CP tests pass; the wider suites fail only 22 tests, which fail identically on unmodified main against the same tree (Megatron FSDP config, hybrid-model FLOPs, MTP freezing).
- **Two-GPU smoke** (`--tiny-model`) with both schedulers: table above.
- **Full recipe** on eight GB200 GPUs with dynamic and static CP: table above.
- `ruff 0.9.9` check and format clean.

- docs: `docs/training/dynamic-context-parallel.md`, long-context example README

+# Dynamic Context Parallel
+
+Dynamic context parallelism (dynamic CP) runs every packed microbatch on a
+context-parallel group sized for its longest sequence, instead of splitting
+every microbatch across the full `context_parallel_size` group. It builds on
+[global-batch online packing](packed-sequences.md#global-batch-online-packing):
+the packing scheduler already sees the whole global batch across data-parallel
+ranks, and with dynamic CP it also picks a context-parallel group for each
+packed bin from the pool of `data_parallel_size x context_parallel_size` ranks.
+
+Dynamic CP needs the Megatron-Core `dev` submodule pin:
+
+```bash
+./scripts/switch_mcore.sh dev && uv sync
+```
+
+`ConfigContainer.validate` reports what an older pin is missing.
+
+## When to Use It
+
+Static context parallelism is sized for the longest sequence a run must fit.
+On a variable-length stream most sequences are much shorter, and splitting them
+across the whole group adds context-parallel communication and smaller kernels
+without needing the memory. Dynamic CP pays off when both of these hold:
+
+- Static CP is required by memory for the long tail. A large vocabulary can
+  make the logits buffer the limit, for example.
+- The stream has a meaningful share of sequences short enough to run on one GPU
+  or a small group.
+
+When nearly every sequence needs the full group, dynamic CP matches static CP up
+to a small scheduling overhead.
+
+## How It Works
+
+`model.max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` is the token capacity of one rank in one
+microbatch. With `default_dynamic_cp`, a sequence of at most that length runs on
+one GPU, a sequence of up to twice that length on a two-GPU group, and so on up
+to the whole pool. The scheduler forms bins longest first and gives each bin a
+power-of-two group, and every rank runs the same number of microbatches in a
+step.
+
+Bridge wires this through the global-batch packing path:
+
+- `model.dynamic_context_parallel=True` makes validation select the
+  `default_dynamic_cp` scheduler instead of `dp_balanced`.
+- The packed batch fetch receives the dynamic-CP flag and returns a
+  `PackedSeqParams` that carries the microbatch's context-parallel group, which
+  attention and rotary embeddings use in place of the static group.
+- The per-sequence alignment multiple covers every group the pool can form:
+  `2 x dp x cp`, and also `dp x cp x tp` under sequence parallelism.
+
+## Configuration
+
+```python
+cfg.dataset.enable_global_batch_packing = True
+cfg.dataset.dataloader_type = "single"
+cfg.model.context_parallel_size = 4  # static CP domain inside each data-parallel replica
+cfg.model.dynamic_context_parallel = True
+cfg.model.min_dynamic_context_parallel_size = 1
+cfg.model.max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank = cfg.model.seq_length // 4
+cfg.model.calculate_per_token_loss = True
+cfg.ddp.average_in_collective = False
+cfg.train.micro_batch_size = 1
+```
+
+Validation applies every global-batch packing rule and adds these:
+
+- The `dp x cp` pool is a power of two with at least two ranks.
+- `min_dynamic_context_parallel_size` is a power of two no larger than the pool.
+- `dist.use_decentralized_pg=False`, because Megatron-Core resolves dynamic
+  groups from its global parallel state.
+- The pool times `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` covers `seq_length`.
+
+## Reference Recipe
+
+`qwen35_text_35b_a3b_sft_8gpu_gb200_bf16_dynamic_cp_config` fine-tunes
+Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on CoderForge-Preview SWE-Rebench trajectories with TP1, PP1,
+CP4, and EP8 on eight GB200 GPUs and a 32K-token cap.
+`examples/training_features/long_context/qwen35_35b_a3b_dynamic_cp.py` launches
+it. Add these overrides for the static-CP baseline on the same packing path:
+
+```bash
+model.dynamic_context_parallel=false model.sequence_packing_scheduler=dp_balanced
+```
+
+On the recipe's own data, about nine in ten CoderForge trajectories exceed the
+32K cap, so nearly every packed sequence needs the full CP4 group. There,
+dynamic CP runs within noise of static CP4: a median step of 88 s against
+83 s, at about 90 model TFLOP/s per GPU. The example's README lists the
+measurements, including the effect of loader workers and recompute choices.
+Expect gains on streams where a meaningful share of sequences is short enough
+to run on one GPU or a small group.
+
+## Models with Wide Attention Heads
+
+Transformer Engine does not train with cuDNN fused attention at head dimension
+256 on Blackwell, so Qwen3.5 attention runs on FlashAttention. FlashAttention
+rejects THD bins that contain padding between sequences. Such models need two
+changes:
+
+- `fold_alignment_padding=True` on the dataset config, which reports each
+  sequence's alignment padding as part of that sequence. The padding stays
+  loss-masked and follows the sequence's last token, so causal attention and
+  recurrent layers compute the same outputs for real tokens.
+- A Megatron-Core that derives `pad_between_seqs` from the actual `cu_seqlens`,
+  proposed in [Megatron-LM #7417](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7417).
+
+Leave `fold_alignment_padding` off for head dimensions of 128 or less, where
+cuDNN fused attention handles the padding itself.
+
+## Practical Caveats
+
+- The first step that uses a new group size pays communicator and kernel setup,
+  so expect a few slow early steps.
+- The scheduler may place short sequences on larger groups to keep every rank
+  busy, so fewer sequences run on one GPU than the length histogram suggests.
+- Transformer Engine's FusedAdam draws parameter handles from a pool of roughly
+  20,000. Many experts on few expert-parallel ranks can exhaust it with the
+  precision-aware optimizer. Use more expert-parallel ranks, as the recipe does
+  with EP8, or offload part of the optimizer to the CPU.
+- The fused cross-entropy materializes an fp32 buffer of tokens per rank times
+  vocabulary size. At a 248K vocabulary this buffer sets
+  `max_seqlen_per_dp_cp_rank` and makes context parallelism necessary at long
+  caps.
+
+## Related Docs
+
+- [Packed Sequences](packed-sequences.md)
+- [Hierarchical Context Parallel](hierarchical-context-parallel.md)
+- [Activation Recomputation](activation-recomputation.md)

+  nearly every packed sequence needs the full CP4 group and dynamic CP has no
